title: Tale of the Falcon and the Partridge (Português)

keywords: tale of the falcon and the partridge
full_text:
Upon the crags of a rocky mountain perched a royal falcon with feathers of iron-grey and eyes like burnished amber. From his dizzying height, he looked down upon a gentle gray partridge that was pecking seeds among the stones of the valley.

The falcon swept down with a rush of wind, pinned the partridge beneath his talons, and mocked him: 'Look at you, frail bird! You spend your life scratching in the dirt, terrified of every shadow, while I soar among the thunderclouds and feast from the wrist of kings!'

The partridge trembled, but spoke with quiet dignity: 'O noble hunter, do not boast of your strength. You fly high, yet a bird in the clouds is visible to all, while the creature of the earth knows how to find refuge among the stones.'

The falcon laughed scornfully: 'What refuge could hide you from my piercing gaze? Watch how I strike down any prey that dares defy me!'

To display his magnificent aerial prowess before delivering the final blow, the falcon released the partridge, leaped into the air, and began climbing in great spirals toward the clouds. He folded his wings, plunged like a lightning bolt toward the valley floor, aiming to seize the partridge in mid-flight with a spectacular dive.

However, the partridge slipped quietly beneath the overhanging ledge of a granite boulder, blending perfectly with the mottled grey stone. The swooping falcon, blinded by the sun and intoxicated by his own speed, could not check his downward momentum. He struck the solid rock face with tremendous force, breaking his wings and shattering his talons.

The humble partridge stepped out from beneath the ledge, looked at the fallen hunter with pity, and said: 'He who flies too high on the wings of pride will find the earth unyielding when he falls.' The partridge flew safely into the thicket, leaving the humbled bird of prey to reflect on the virtue of modest quietude.
moral: Boastful arrogance invites disaster, while humble discretion preserves life and safety. [PT]
